parsed.explanation: No visitor-facing exposure is documented: recognition is declaration-based, discrimination in goods, services and healthcare is prohibited, "change of sex" is a hate-crime aggravator, and there is no criminal offence, facility ban, border mismatch rule, or police profiling. Custody placement follows disclosed identity on a case-by-case basis with dignity safeguards (honoured forms of address) and no codified birth-sex rule — the only subnational item, and a positive one. Nonbinary markers unavailable and unaddressed conversion practices/sex-characteristic protection are resident-facing gaps that do not touch a traveller carrying home documents. This is a well-documented jurisdiction; the absence of any reported trans-visitor harm or targeting is therefore a moderately positive signal. What holds it below the 0.85 tier is that enforcement outcomes (hotel refusals corrected, prosecutions, border practice) are not demonstrated — protections are largely on paper — plus minor uncertainty on nonbinary passport acceptance and custody edge cases. Strong legal framework, no documented hostility, but unproven operating remedies.
